title: The Wisdom of Ben Sira
subtitle: Sirach Introduction — Who Was Ben Sira and Why Study This Book?
description: Meet Jesus Ben Sira, the sage of Jerusalem whose collected wisdom spans the breadth of godly living. Discover why the early church treasured this book and what the Puritans found valuable in its counsel on fearing God, governing the tongue, and walking uprightly.

title: The Crown of Wisdom
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 1–2 — True Wisdom Begins with the Fear of the Lord
description: Sirach opens with a majestic hymn declaring that all wisdom comes from God alone. Walk through chapters 1 and 2 to discover how reverential fear becomes the root, fullness, and crown of wisdom — and how patient trust sustains the faithful in trial.

title: A Son's Duty, A Father's Blessing
subtitle: Sirach Chapter 3 — The Sacred Duties Owed to Father and Mother
description: Sirach chapter 3 expands the fifth commandment with tender and searching counsel on honoring aging parents, the blessings that flow from filial piety, and the spiritual danger of neglecting those who raised us in the fear of the Lord.

title: The Lowly Heart Before God
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 4–5 — Walking in Humility and Patient Trust
description: Ben Sira teaches that the humble soul finds favor with God and man. Explore Sirach chapters 4 and 5 on the blessings of lowliness, the danger of presumption, and why the patient spirit outweighs the proud heart in every season of life.

title: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence
subtitle: Sirach Chapter 6 — The Value and Testing of True Friendship
description: Sirach 6 contains some of the most penetrating counsel on friendship ever written. Learn how Ben Sira distinguishes fair-weather companions from faithful friends, why friendship must be tested in adversity, and how the fear of God binds souls together.

title: Bridling the Tongue and the Passions
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 18–19 — Mastering Self-Control Through Wisdom
description: Ben Sira turns his attention to the disciplines of self-governance. Study Sirach 18 and 19 on thinking before speaking, restraining desire, and the destructive power of gossip — with deep echoes of James and the Proverbs on the unruly tongue.

title: The Grace of the Table
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 31–32 — Moderation, Generosity, and the Art of Hospitality
description: Sirach offers remarkably practical counsel on eating, drinking, and hosting with grace. Explore chapters 31 and 32 on the spiritual danger of gluttony, the beauty of moderation, and how the godly household extends hospitality as an act of worship.

title: The Sacrifice That Pleases God
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 34–35 — True Prayer, Worship, and Righteous Offering
description: What does God truly desire in worship? Sirach chapters 34 and 35 expose the emptiness of ritual without righteousness and call the faithful to offer prayer, praise, and charity from a sincere heart — themes that echo through the prophets and the Psalms.

title: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men
subtitle: Sirach Chapters 44–50 — The Heroes of Faith from Enoch to Simon
description: In one of the most celebrated passages of ancient literature, Ben Sira walks through the great heroes of Israel's history — from Enoch and Noah to Moses, David, Elijah, and the high priest Simon. Discover how this gallery of faith foreshadows Hebrews 11.

title: A Sage's Farewell Prayer
subtitle: Sirach Chapter 51 — Ben Sira's Personal Thanksgiving and Wisdom Hymn
description: The Book of Sirach closes with a deeply personal prayer of thanksgiving and an alphabetic hymn inviting all to seek wisdom. Walk through chapter 51 as Ben Sira recounts God's deliverance, offers praise, and bids farewell with a final call to the house of learning.
